fot_token_is_dispute_token.meaning: the configured disputeToken is a fee-on-transfer token

dispute_amount_sent.meaning: disputeAmount tokens the user sends in disputeTree() (illustrative 1000)

fot_fee_deducted.meaning: the FoT token deducts a transfer fee on the deposit (illustrative 1% = 10 tokens)

no_recovery_path.meaning: recoverERC20 cannot clear disputer and further deposits do not help because FoT fees apply on outgoing transfers; only upgrade/migration recovers

disputer_stuck_nonzero.meaning: disputer remains permanently set to the original non-zero address because resolveDispute() always reverts and is the only function that clears it

assumptions: disputeTree() deposit succeeds and records the full disputeAmount while the contract receives fewer tokens.
resolveDispute() is the only function that clears the disputer field.
The FoT fee percentage is illustrative (1%), not a fixed protocol parameter.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether disputeTree() itself succeeds or reverts on the FoT deposit; only the received amount is described.
Whether the governor or disputer triggers resolveDispute() is not fixed; both branches are described.

limitations: The exact disputeAmount and FoT fee are illustrative examples, not fixed protocol parameters; the plan uses symbolic quantities.
The relation is expressed as a Boolean outcome because the report states the stuck-disputer condition qualitatively without a numeric definition.
Only the disputer_stuck_nonzero impact is formalized here; other reported impacts are handled in separate claim-generation passes.
